name: V60 dripper
description: A cone-shaped dripper with a large single hole and spiral ridges that let water flow through at a controlled rate, giving you more control over extraction than flat-bottomed drippers.

name: Paper filter
description: Traps oils and fine particles, producing a cleaner, lighter-bodied cup than metal filters or immersion brewing.

name: AeroPress paper filter
description: A small round filter sized specifically for the AeroPress cap — regular pour-over filters won't fit.

name: Gooseneck kettle
description: A kettle with a narrow, curved spout that gives precise control over pour speed and placement, which matters for even saturation in pour-over brewing.

name: Digital scale
description: Weighing coffee and water (rather than using volume scoops) is the biggest single lever for consistent, repeatable brews.

name: Server or mug
description: Any vessel that sits under the brewer to catch coffee as it drains.

name: Burr grinder
description: Crushes beans between two abrasive surfaces for a consistent particle size, unlike blade grinders which chop unevenly and produce a mix of fines and boulders.

name: French press
description: A cylindrical brewer with a mesh plunger. Coffee steeps fully immersed in water, then the plunger separates grounds from liquid.

name: Stirring spoon
description: Used to break up the crust of grounds that forms during immersion brewing and to stir in the water evenly.

name: Kettle
description: Any kettle that can heat water to a controlled temperature — a gooseneck spout isn't necessary when precise pour placement doesn't matter, like in a French press.

name: AeroPress
description: A plastic press brewer that combines immersion steeping with pressure filtration through a paper filter, producing a clean, fast cup.

name: Stirring paddle
description: A flat paddle (often included with the AeroPress) for stirring grounds without splashing.

name: Moka pot
description: A stovetop brewer with three chambers — water heats in the base, builds pressure, and pushes up through coffee grounds and into the top chamber.

name: Stove or heat source
description: Any stovetop burner or induction plate capable of a steady medium-low heat.

name: Large jar or cold brew maker
description: Any large, sealable vessel works for cold brew — dedicated cold brew makers just add a built-in filter for convenience.

name: Fine mesh strainer or paper filter
description: Removes coarse grounds after a long cold steep; a paper filter afterward removes remaining fine sediment for a cleaner concentrate.

name: Espresso machine
description: Forces hot water through finely-ground, tamped coffee at high pressure (roughly 9 bar), producing a concentrated shot with crema.

name: Espresso grinder
description: A grinder capable of very fine, consistent particle sizes — espresso is far more sensitive to grind size than other methods, so a dedicated or high-quality grinder matters more here.

name: Tamper
description: Compresses grounds evenly in the portafilter basket so water passes through them uniformly instead of finding the path of least resistance.

name: Portafilter
description: The handled basket that holds the dose of grounds and locks into the espresso machine's group head.
